transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately I can’t think straight at work—decisions that used to be easy now leave me stuck and second‑guessing everything. My HR partner suggested an occupational medicine consult after a performance check-in about my recent decline in concentration, which led to this referral. I just can't seem to keep up with tasks that used to be manageable.
Along with these concentration difficulties, have you also been experiencing a persistently low mood or a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes, for the past few weeks it’s felt like this heavy, gray film has settled over everything. I constantly catch myself staring at my spreadsheets or out the hotel window feeling utterly hollow and on the verge of tears for no clear reason. It has made it incredibly hard to feel any interest or joy in anything lately.
Have you recently gone through any major life changes, losses, or highly stressful events before these symptoms started?

Yes, I was recently promoted to lead a high-visibility lean transformation project across several of our plants. It came with a lot of intense pressure, including frequent travel, late-night calls with overseas vendors, and aggressive cost-savings targets. The constant stress and sleep disruption from this new role really seem to have triggered and worsened these swings for me.
Besides your work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday areas of your life, and is this worry difficult to control?

No, not really. My worries are almost entirely focused on my work and how much my job performance has slipped lately. I don't find myself worrying about other everyday areas of my life, just this project and my career.
Along with the low mood and concentration issues, have you been feeling unusually fatigued or lacking in energy, even when you haven't done much physical activity?

Yes, I feel completely exhausted and drained of energy. Even simple things like typing an email feel like they require immense physical effort, as if I'm moving underwater. To make it worse, I lie in bed exhausted but wired at night, and I always wake up feeling entirely unrefreshed.
Have you also been experiencing feelings of worthlessness, or have you been blaming yourself excessively for things that may be out of your control?

I wouldn't say I feel worthless or that I'm blaming myself for things out of my control. But I do feel incredibly frustrated and stuck because of how hard it's become to make simple decisions and keep up with my workload.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite, such as losing interest in food or eating much less than usual?

Yes, my appetite has dropped significantly. I used to love suggesting new places for team dinners, but lately, even after a 12-hour workday, I just pick at a few bites and push the food around. I have no real interest in eating, and I've noticed my clothes are starting to hang looser on me.
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or felt that life is no longer worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt that life isn't worth living. While I do feel extremely hollow, exhausted, and completely overwhelmed by my work situation, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
Exactly how long have you been experiencing this low mood, lack of interest, and low energy on a daily basis?
This current low spell has been dragging on for about three months now. It started right around the time the most intense phase of the lean transformation project rollout began.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of low mood, exhaustion, and loss of interest at any other time in your life, perhaps during a less stressful period?

Yes, looking back, I've been cycling through these highs and crashes since my mid-twenties. I used to dismiss the low stretches where work felt like wading through mud as just normal reactions to project cycles, but this pattern has actually been going on for years. It has just never been this severe or hard to ignore until now.

During those 'high' periods you mentioned, did you experience times where you felt extremely energetic, needed much less sleep than usual, or had racing thoughts? How long did those periods of high energy typically last?

Yes, during those highs I felt incredibly energetic and active, constantly volunteering for extra tasks and even pacing my hotel room at midnight. I only slept three or four hours a night but woke up feeling completely refreshed, and I talked so fast that coworkers joked I was on "1.5x speed." These periods usually lasted for a few weeks before I eventually crashed.
During those high periods, did your behavior ever cause significant problems at work or in your relationships, or lead you to take risks you normally wouldn't?

I didn't take extreme risks like reckless spending, but my behavior during those highs definitely caused friction at work. I would snap at my team over tiny delays during meetings, dominate conversations by talking at "1.5x speed" without letting others speak, and over-commit to too many initiatives and after-work activities. All of that over-scheduling and intensity ultimately contributed to my crash.
Have these periods of high energy or the low crashes ever been triggered by medications, alcohol, or other substances, or did they happen completely on their own?
No, I don't think they were ever triggered by medications, alcohol, or any substances. They seem to happen completely on their own, though they definitely get intensified by work stress and pressure.
Despite these difficulties, are you still able to perform your daily work and household tasks to some extent, or have you become almost completely unable to function?

My ability to function at work has severely declined; I've missed deadlines and had to hand off parts of my flagship project to colleagues. My manager has even hinted that they might reconsider my role on the team if things don't improve soon. Even simple, routine decisions now leave me completely stuck and second-guessing myself, making normal functioning incredibly difficult.
